PlayStation GTA 6 Leak Ban: What Is Confirmed [2026]
articles.chapeau: PlayStation reportedly banned an account over a GTA 6 leak shared in PS App messaging. See what Sony policy confirms and what stays unverified.
articles.txt:
Sofia Lindström November 3, 2026 11 min read A PlayStation account was reportedly banned after its owner shared a Grand Theft Auto VI leak through PlayStation App messaging, according to a Notebookcheck report that the gaming press picked up on November 3, 2026. The core rule behind any such action is public: PlayStation’s player behaviour guidelines say Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) may suspend accounts, temporarily or permanently, for breaching its Terms of Service or Code of Conduct.
The report has a gap, and we will flag it early. Sony has not publicly confirmed this specific ban. Nor have Rockstar Games, Take-Two Interactive, or the account holder. The identity of the user, the message that was shared, the date, the length of the ban, and the type of penalty all remain unconfirmed. That makes this a reported story with a documented policy behind it, not a verified enforcement case.
Still, the timing matters. GTA VI is scheduled for November 19, 2026, which leaves 16 days, and leaked footage has dominated the conversation for weeks. Rockstar has already described its position on the flood of clips in our earlier report on the studio’s reaction to the leaks . This analysis covers what the PlayStation story claims, what Sony’s rules allow, how Take-Two is attacking the leak chain from another angle, and what each side stands to gain or lose.

Notebookcheck reported that a PlayStation user lost access after passing GTA VI leak material to another person through the messaging feature inside the PlayStation App. The headline claim is simple. A private-feeling channel did not shield the sender from platform enforcement.
The fact sheet we are working from is strict about what holds up. The confirmed pieces come from Sony’s own published policy and from Take-Two’s legal filings, not from the ban itself. The ban is the unconfirmed piece. We therefore treat the story as a credible report that fits Sony’s stated rules, and nothing more until Sony, Rockstar, Take-Two, or the user says otherwise.
Sony’s framework gives it two broad levers. It can suspend an account for a set period, or it can end the account’s access permanently. Either route follows a breach of the Terms of Service or the Code of Conduct. The company states this outright on its support pages, and it applies the same language to every player, from a first-time violator to a repeat offender.
The difference matters for this story. A communication suspension restricts social features, including interaction with other players and online play. A full suspension goes further. The Notebookcheck report does not say which one hit the user, and that missing detail changes how severe the penalty looks. Losing chat is an annoyance. Losing an account tied to a digital library is a financial hit.
PlayStation generally emails suspended users with the reason and the duration of the suspension. If the leak ban is real, the account holder holds the best primary evidence, because that email would name the policy and the term. Until that message surfaces, every detail about length and scope is guesswork.
Many players assume a one-to-one message is private in the way a phone call is private. Sony’s process says otherwise. PlayStation states that reported content may be reviewed by moderators. If the content breaches the Code of Conduct, it may be removed, and action may follow against the account that shared it.
That sequence shows how a ban over a messaged clip could happen without any proactive snooping. A recipient flags the message. A moderator reads the report. The content gets measured against the rules. Nothing in the confirmed policy points to bulk scanning of private messages for leaks, and nothing in the Notebookcheck report claims it. The likelier path is a user report, though that remains our inference, not a confirmed fact.
The distinction matters for privacy debates. A report-driven system punishes sharing that someone else objects to. A scanning system would watch everyone. The first model is common across platforms. The second would spark a much louder fight, and no evidence in this case suggests Sony runs it.

articles.txt:
If you want to play GTA 6 on the PS5 when it launches on November 19, you’ll need about 210 GB of free storage. Lexar is offering the 1-TB version of the PS5 SSD EQ790 with a heat sink at a discounted price through November 30, 2026: Use the code LXDEGOGTA6 on Amazon to get 5 percent off the regular price of 209.99 euros. That brings the price down to about 199.49 euros.
This figure does not come from Rockstar, but from the X account PlayStation Game Size, which regularly retrieves download sizes from the PlayStation Store’s backend. In late October, the account cited 210 GB for the Standard Edition on the PS5 . The account has a good track record, but this is still a leak. A day-one patch and subsequent updates for the online mode will likely be added on top of that. The preload is set to begin one week before release, on November 12.
For comparison: Depending on the version, GTA 5 takes up around 100 GB on the PS5, while Red Dead Redemption 2 takes up around 150 GB. And here’s how much free space the consoles actually have:
So on a launch-generation PS5, GTA 6 takes up nearly a third of the storage. If you’ve also installed Call of Duty, Fortnite, and one or two Sony exclusives, you’ll need to free up space or upgrade. With a 210 GB download, it’s worth taking a quick look at your internet connection. If it’s acting up, our tips can help you resolve internet issues on the PS5 .
The EQ790 is an M.2-2280 SSD with a PCIe 4.0 x4 interface. Lexar unveiled the heatsink version in August 2025; it’s available in 1, 2, and 4 TB capacities. The 1-TB version is on sale.
The 7,000 MB/s is significantly higher than the 5,500 MB/s recommended by Sony for a PS5 expansion. In practice, the console loads games from such an SSD just as quickly as from the internal storage. Sony itself points out that not every game achieves exactly the same performance, but with current Gen 4 models, the difference is barely noticeable.
It’s important to note that the EQ790 is a DRAM-less SSD. Instead of its own cache chip, it uses a small portion of the system’s RAM via HMB. For games that primarily involve reading data, this hardly matters. During large, prolonged write operations (such as copying 200 GB in one go), a DRAM-less SSD tends to slow down more quickly once the cache is exhausted than a more expensive model. The advantage: Lexar claims up to 40 percent lower power consumption compared to Gen4 SSDs with DRAM.
Yes. Sony allows a maximum total height of 11.25 mm in the expansion slot, including the heatsink, with no more than 8 mm protruding above the circuit board. The EQ790, with its pre-mounted heatsink, measures 9.7 mm and thus stays within the limits. You don’t need to buy a separate heatsink or attach anything.
Installation takes about ten minutes: Turn off the console, remove the cover, unscrew the bay plate, insert the SSD, and screw it into place using the appropriate spacer. The next time you boot up, the PS5 will format the SSD and test its speed. Sony describes the steps in detail on its official support page . After that, you can install GTA 6 directly onto the new SSD or move older games to it.
According to Lexar, the code is valid from November 1 through November 30, 2026. A note on the price: Amazon prices fluctuate, and the 1-TB version has been available for well under 200 euros at times in recent months. So it doesn’t hurt to take a quick look at the price history. At the same time, SSD prices have risen noticeably in 2026, so a bargain from the past isn’t a given anymore.

articles.t: Mass Effect Flag Cuts Unverified; GTA VI Nov. 19 [2026]
articles.chapeau: BioWare flag-edit claim lacks confirmation, while GTA VI preload starts Nov. 12 and launch is Nov. 19. Here is what is verified and what is not.
articles.txt:
Elias Virtanen November 3, 2026 12 min read Two stories dominated the gaming news cycle heading into November. One is a claim that BioWare trimmed extremist flags from a new Mass Effect presentation. The other is the countdown to Grand Theft Auto VI, which Rockstar Games lists for November 19, 2026. A weekly roundup from iXBT.games bundled both under a headline saying BioWare cut the flags and that GTA VI is ready.
That headline mixes one claim that nobody has confirmed with one date that Rockstar itself publishes. This analysis separates the two. It lays out what is verified, what rests on unnamed media, and what players should do in the 16 days between today and launch. If you want the longer ledger of facts versus rumors, our GTA 6 confirmed-versus-rumor scorecard tracks it item by item.
The short version: the GTA VI release date, the two launch platforms and the preload date are solid. The Mass Effect flag story and the idea that development is finished are not. Treat them differently, and you avoid repeating something that may not survive its first official response.

Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
The report in question says BioWare removed extremist or banned flags from a presentation tied to the new Mass Effect. That is the whole claim. It comes from the iXBT.games weekly digest, which attributes the information to unnamed media rather than to a studio statement, a leaked document or a named developer.
Several details are missing. The reporting does not identify which flags were removed or how many. It does not name the presentation or the event where it appeared. It does not explain who made the edit, when it happened, or why. Anyone who tells you the motivation is known has gone past what the source says.
That gap matters because flag imagery is a sensitive area for any game with real-world parallels. Studios routinely scrub symbols that could break local laws or invite harassment, especially in material shown to the press or at trade events. A quiet edit of that kind would be ordinary housekeeping. A reader hearing “extremist flags” without context could picture something far more dramatic, which is why the lack of detail deserves attention.
As of November 3, neither BioWare nor Electronic Arts has published a statement confirming the removal. No studio blog post, no press office reply and no developer social post appears in the available research. The only trail leads back to the unnamed media cited in the iXBT.games digest.
The title of the presentation is also unconfirmed. Some aggregator summaries attach a specific product name to it, but no official source establishes one, so this article does not repeat it. The same goes for any quote circulating under the line “it is ready.” Nobody is identified as the speaker, and no verifiable source backs the wording.
A claim built on unnamed media can still be true. It simply cannot be checked by readers, which means the burden stays with whoever repeats it. Three tests help. Does a named outlet stand behind it? Does a primary source, such as the studio, confirm it? Can the details be cross-checked? The Mass Effect flag story passes none of these today, so it belongs in the “reported, unconfirmed” column until BioWare or EA responds.
It also helps to remember where BioWare stands. Our earlier coverage of the Battlefront III decision and the BioWare closure reports showed how much speculation clings to this studio. Every new Mass Effect rumor lands in a climate where readers already expect upheaval, and that makes careful sourcing more important, not less.
The firm ground starts here. Rockstar’s official Grand Theft Auto VI page lists the game as “Coming November 19, 2026.” That is first-party wording, published by the studio, and it is the anchor for everything else in this piece.
The platforms are equally settled. The game targets PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at launch. articles.t: PlayStation reportedly bans account for GTA 6 leak shared in PS App messaging
articles.chapeau: The PS App may be one of the riskiest places to share leaked GTA 6 gameplay videos. A Reddit user claims a friend is facing a permanent PSN suspension after posting a clip. Sony has implemented more automated monitoring to detect violations during chats.
articles.txt:
Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar have requested DMCA takedowns of GTA 6 leaks on social media. Sony also appears to be monitoring the PS App for unauthorized footage. Redditor Silver-Succotash-612 alleges an acquaintance’s PlayStation account suffered a ban after sharing a video.
According to the poster, a companion tried to send the GTA 6 gameplay clip , possibly from Cyberleek , to a contact. The PSN profile was frozen immediately, prompting a support request . They learned an appeal would take 3 months, making regaining access in the near term unlikely.
Gamers should take the claim with a grain of salt, but bans have happened after posting TOS-breaking content. In one example, a user uploaded a Conan Exiles screenshot depicting nude characters in a private group chat. That individual saw their PlayStation account banned for 30 days.
What’s unique about the Redditor’s story is the prompt and severe punitive action. Normally, Sony employees don’t investigate potential violations unless a gamer reports them. In this case, only two friends were discussing a GTA 6 leak in the PS App.
Automated monitoring may explain the gameplay clip’s instant detection. In March 2025, the console maker introduced Nudge, which detects and warns chatters about inappropriate messages. Even so, support still isn't supposed to view communications or restrict a PlayStation account without a report.
Another scenario is that PlayStation has taken special precautions ahead of the GTA 6 release date . Rockstar and Sony have signed a lucrative marketing deal . The PS5 game can attract massive numbers of new customers to the hardware’s ecosystem. Leaks spoiling announcements could damage both companies.
Most observers agree Silver-Succotash-612’s friend should have found an alternative to the PS App. Cyberleek’s videos spread through platforms less susceptible to DMCA strikes. Regardless, some readers raised privacy concerns and questioned the justification for an indefinite ban.

articles.t: Why HR should care about Grand Theft Auto VI
articles.chapeau: This isn’t the first time a pop culture phenomenon has tanked worker output.
articles.txt:
This isn’t the first time a pop culture phenomenon has tanked worker output.
NOW PLAYING is HR Dive Reporter Caroline Colvin’s column at the intersection of HR and entertainment.
Gamers have been waiting for Grand Theft Auto VI for what feels like forever — and that heated anticipation may have negative repercussions for the workplace.
GTA 6, as it’s colloquially called, officially drops on Nov. 19, 2026, with pre-loading starting on Nov. 12. Because of this, HR may see time-off requests — yes, really — as early as this week, if they haven’t approved PTO already.
According to an October report from Zety, 11% of workers are planning to take time off for GTA 6 or tweak their schedules. The data shows it’s more common among younger workers compared to older workers and more so among men than women to make these schedule adjustments.
Zety is only the latest source to claim that gamers’ return to Vice City will be bad for productivity. Back in September, Steven Adams of the Houston Rockets said even the NBA’s performance would plummet because of GTA 6 in November. Adams’ prediction may actually be supported, too, by a recent Money.com report suggesting that Nov. 19 will be a “ billion-dollar sick day ” thanks to GTA 6.
While 1 in 10 workers being OOO or AFK for GTA probably wasn’t on HR’s bingo card for the year, 9% of respondents told Zety that they have taken PTO for a video game before. The survey also polled workers about a variety of entertainment events, with workers revealing that they’re not always going to request time off; they may just call in “sick.”
HR has experienced that phenomenon before. After the Super Bowl, millions of people call in sick the following Monday. Historically, March Madness has been a workplace distraction for the ages, though this ongoing tournament in particular has sometimes been used to re-engage burnt-out employees .
What should HR do about GTA 6? I think they should take a similarly positive, proactive approach.
I, like many, see workers as fully realized people and think they should take time off for whatever they need. I’m inspired by my own team in this area, with my fellow HR Dive team members not just taking time off for illness or emergencies, but for homeroom parties, family vacations, sporting events, concerts and yes, even video game releases.
PTO should be used freely, not for the sake of frivolity, but because it allows people to show up at work as individuals. It also gives them a chance to recharge and return to work with renewed energy. With this in mind, HR should get out ahead of whatever they think may hurt worker productivity in the short term — be it GTA 6 now or Jay-Z’s Super Bowl soon — to bolster worker productivity in the long term.
It’s much better to have a game plan that accommodates everyone’s desires than to be caught short-staffed that day.

Golden path So GTA 6 is getting really close now and while there’s still so much that is secret about it, I can’t help but start fantasising about playing it and what I’ll do. Because we don’t know much concrete it’s hard to say I’ll go there and do that, but my plan is to ignore the story as soon as possible and go off exploring.
I particularly like the more wilderness areas in GTA 5 and open world games in general, so I’ll be heading to the everglades and that mud tournament place. I really liked the outdoors area in the leaked Cyberleek footage (whatever happened to them?) and will have great fun messing around there.
The city I’ll probably leave till later, but I do get the feeling, from what we’ve been shown that my idea of skipping the story is kind of built into this one. I think it’s what a lot of people do in open world games and the impression I get from previews is that doing robberies is a lot more up to you than part of a story mission, perhaps to make the whole thing more freefrom.
Anyway, interested to know what other people are planning? Will you go for the story path and then explore more or do it my way? Paulie

articles.t: Is GTA 6 Safe for Kids? Rated M 17+ Parent Guide [2026]
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 is rated M (Mature 17+). See what earns the rating, what parents should know, and which parental controls to set before your teen plays. Updated 2026.
articles.txt:
Marcus Chen November 3, 2026 13 min read Rockstar Games ships Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, and the first question in many households is simple: is GTA 6 appropriate for kids ? A Local12 (WKRC) report frames the launch as the end of a 13-year wait and pairs it with that parenting question. The answer on the platform listings is blunt. Xbox rates the game MATURE 17+ and flags it as potentially inappropriate for children.
That rating arrives with eight content descriptors, a $79.99 standard price, and a $99.99 Ultimate Edition. With 16 days left before launch, this analysis walks through what is confirmed, what is only reported, and what parents can do before a console box or a digital code lands under the tree. For the wider picture of what Rockstar has and has not confirmed, our GTA 6 confirmed-versus-rumor scorecard separates fact from chatter.
· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
No. The game is not built for children, and the official listing says so in plain language. Xbox’s store page for Grand Theft Auto VI carries the MATURE 17+ rating, lists the content descriptors, and marks the title as potentially inappropriate for children. Parents who read only one line of the listing should read that one.
The headline framing that the game follows 13 years of anticipation comes from news coverage, not from a Rockstar statement we could locate. We treat that figure as the press framing of the wait and not as an official Rockstar claim. The rating, the date, the platforms, and the prices are a different category. Those details appear on storefront listings and are the facts this article builds on.
Two practical points follow. First, a 17+ rating is guidance from the storefront and the rating system, not a law that stops a 13-year-old from touching a controller. Second, the burden shifts to parents, because a game this heavily anticipated will be everywhere at once: in group chats, on streams, and on lunch tables. Waiting for the topic to come up is a weaker plan than raising it before launch day.
The confirmed release date is November 19, 2026. The confirmed platforms are PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The standard edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition costs $99.99, a $20 gap. Rockstar’s own Newswire remains the place where the studio posts official announcements, and the PlayStation store page mirrors the console-side listing.
The two-tier price structure matters for family budgets. A parent weighing a gift is looking at either $79.99 or $99.99 for a single title, before any extra storage or a subscription. Retail promotions already tied to the launch, such as the Walmart pre-order bundle at $79.99 with a mystery bag , show how hard the market is pushing the game toward impulse buys. A high price tag does not equal a high age bar, and a store sale does not equal a green light from the rating system.
The Xbox listing for Grand Theft Auto VI names eight content descriptors. That is a long list, and it is worth reading item by item, because each one tells a parent something different. The listing confirms the labels. The right-hand column below is our plain-language reading of what each label generally signals for a household, not a description of specific scenes.
Seven of the eight descriptors concern what a child would see and hear. The eighth, In-Game Purchases, concerns what a child could spend. Parents often treat the last item as a footnote. It deserves equal weight because a saved card on a family console can turn a curious teen into a surprise bill within one evening.
Count the flags first, then read the strongest ones. A single descriptor can describe a game that is fine for a mature 15-year-old in some households. A stack of seven content flags is a different signal, because the content categories overlap and compound. Violence, language, and sexual themes in one title mean there is no quiet corner of the game that a parent can assume is safe. Read the list as a whole and decide on the whole.
Compare this descriptor list with the label on a typical teen-rated action game. Teen-rated titles commonly carry a small number of flags, such as fantasy violence or mild language. GTA 6 carries seven content flags plus a purchase notice. The count alone suggests the listing treats this as a clear adult title and not a borderline case.

articles.txt:
Le 27 août 2026, une simple joggeuse de Vice City résume l’ambition de Rockstar Games : faire de chaque PNJ de GTA 6 un corps crédible. Mais ce réalisme inspiré de Red Dead Redemption 2 restera-t-il agréable manette en main ?
Dans le Netflix Extended Look de GTA 6 , diffusé le 27 août 2026, un détail a échappé à beaucoup de monde : le mollet d’une joggeuse PNJ se contracte à chaque foulée sous le soleil de Vice City. Cette simple scène, relevée par la communauté sur Reddit et mise en avant par GamingBible, illustre jusqu’où Rockstar Games peaufine ses personnages non jouables.
Les fans se souviennent encore des chevaux de Red Dead Redemption 2 , dont les muscles, la démarche et même la taille des testicules changeaient avec la température. Avec GTA 6 , tout indique que ce niveau de détail organique s’applique désormais aux humains, dans une mégapole moderne surpeuplée. Reste une question brûlante : les PNJ de Leonida vont-ils réellement dépasser ceux de l’Ouest sauvage de 2018 ?
Techniquement, le saut est vertigineux. Selon RockstarActu, GTA 5 comptait environ 55 000 animations de PNJ, contre 300 000 pour Red Dead Redemption 2 . GTA 6 monterait à près de 600 000 animations issues de la capture de mouvement , avec une densité de foule jusqu’à onze fois supérieure à celle de Los Santos. Cette surenchère sert justement à crédibiliser chaque corps et chaque micro-réaction.
Mais Rockstar ne cherche pas le fétichisme du détail pour le principe. Rob Nelson a expliqué à GamesRadar que le système d’interaction PNJ de Red Dead Redemption 2 revient dans GTA 6 , mais poussé « beaucoup plus loin ». Dans un monde urbain, cela signifie des PNJ de tailles et de morphologies variées, qui marchent, courent, conduisent et paniquent de façon cohérente avec leur physique.
Côté comportement, Rockstar Games généralise le système de « focus » né dans Red Dead Redemption 2 . En visant un PNJ, Jason ou Lucia peut le saluer, le provoquer ou tenter de le calmer. Selon RockstarActu, ces personnages réagissent si vous les suivez trop longtemps ou si vous écoutez leurs conversations : certains s’éloignent, d’autres vous insultent, quelques-uns frappent le premier.
L’Extended Look montre même deux PNJ quittant discrètement une supérette en voyant Jason et Lucia se préparer à un braquage. Pour que ces scènes restent crédibles, Rockstar a ouvert un studio dédié à Los Angeles, épaulé par des équipes à New York et Londres, chargé d’écrire à la main des dialogues d’ambiance uniques. Buzzarena souligne que ces PNJ ne reposent sur aucune IA générative pour leurs répliques.
Cette obsession de l’illusion vivante a pourtant des limites. Numerama rapporte que Rob Nelson reconnaît qu’ »il faut parfois sacrifier le réalisme au profit du confort des joueuses et des joueurs » : un système de courses au supermarché pour remplir le frigo a ainsi été abandonné car trop pesant. Un signal rassurant pour celles et ceux qui trouvaient certaines animations de Red Dead Redemption 2 un peu longues.
Reste à voir si ces promesses tiendront. Une chose est sûre : sueur après une bagarre, portraits de Jason et Lucia qui changent selon leurs tenues ou montres affichant l’heure in-game doivent rendre Leonida crédible sans la rendre pénible à jouer. Réponse le 19 novembre 2026, date de sortie de GTA 6 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S .

articles.t: GTA VI : pourquoi les fans de Red Dead Redemption 2 vont adorer l’intrigue du couple Lucia et Jason ?

articles.txt:
GTA VI : pourquoi les fans de Red Dead Redemption 2 vont adorer l’intrigue du couple Lucia et Jason ? Publié le 2 novembre 2026 à 22 h 00 Par Maxence Grosvalet
© Rockstar Games Dans quelques semaines, le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de l’histoire sera enfin disponible. Mais avant que Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA VI ) ne soit accessible à tous les fans le 19 novembre prochain, les équipes du studio Rockstar continuent de révéler, petit à petit, certains détails concernant leur jeu vidéo. Ainsi, si vous avez adoré l’aventure de Red Dead Redemption 2 , vous risquez de devenir accro à l’intrigue mise en place autour du couple Jason et Lucia.
Il ne reste plus qu’un peu plus de deux semaines d’attente… Dans 17 jours exactement, soit le 19 novembre prochain, les fans du monde entier pourront enfin mettre la main sur le très attendu Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA VI ). Toujours développée par le célèbre studio Rockstar, cette nouvelle aventure va plonger les fans au cœur de Vice City, une ville fictive inspirée de Miami. On y incarnera alors les personnages de Jason et Lucia , une version moderne du célèbre couple Bonnie et Clyde , qui tenteront tant bien que mal de se faire une place dans le milieu criminel de Vice City.
La romance entre Lucia et Jason sera donc un point central de l’histoire du futur GTA VI . Du moins, c’est ce qu’on a voulu nous faire croire… La réalité présente dans le jeu vidéo pourrait toutefois s’avérer bien différente de ce que l’on pensait…
Dès les premiers trailers, l’objectif du studio Rockstar est clair : mettre en avant son duo de protagonistes . Lors de la présentation du 27 août dernier , les équipes avaient notamment insisté sur l’évolution de la relation entre Jason et Lucia, qui fluctuera donc en fonction de vos actions. Dans GTA VI , l’amour est un sentiment qui s’entretient . Vous devrez donc bien penser à faire répondre vos personnages aux textos de l’autre, tout en leur faisant passer quelques activités ensemble pour maintenir la flamme en vie.
Pour autant, est-ce réellement grave si la relation entre Jason et Lucia se termine ? Les deux personnages peuvent-ils se séparer dans le jeu vidéo ? Eh bien, la réponse est non, puis oui. Dans une interview pour Edge Magazine , Rob Nelson, le codirecteur du studio Rockstar, est revenu sur la relation entre ses deux protagonistes : « Au départ, ils veulent être ensemble et donner une nouvelle chance à leur relation. Mais, au fur et à mesure que le jeu progresse, c’est à vous de la garder ou de la perdre . »
En réalité, il n’y a donc aucune incidence sur la façon dont vous souhaitez gérer le couple Jason et Lucia dans GTA VI . Si vous voulez jouer le jeu, vous pouvez entretenir la relation et les garder en couple tout au long de votre aventure, mais si cette partie ne vous intéresse pas, le couple finira par rompre, sans que cela impacte réellement votre aventure. Lucia et Jason deviendront alors de simples partenaires de crime, sans que cela ne pose aucun problème.
Cette volonté du studio, que le joueur puisse influencer le destin amoureux de Jason et Lucia, ne vient toutefois pas de nulle part. Lors de cette même interview, Rob Nelson affirme qu’elle est venue tout droit d’un autre jeu vidéo à succès du studio Rockstar : Red Dead Redemption 2 .
Dans ce jeu vidéo, les fans incarnent Arthur Morgan, un hors-la-loi qui, alors qu’il est en cavale avec sa bande, se retrouve au cœur d’une grande introspection pendant que le monde lui-même change autour de lui. L’âge d’or de l’Ouest Sauvage disparaît peu à peu pour laisser place à l’industrialisation venue de la côte Est. Le joueur doit alors choisir comment Arthur doit dépenser son argent et ses ressources. « Est-ce que je dépense cet argent pour moi, en vêtements stylés, chevaux et selles ? Ou est-ce que je le donne à ma famille adoptive dans le gang ? » explique Rob Nelson, révélant que les joueurs doivent naviguer entre « égoïsme et altruisme » .
Pour la relation entre Jason et Lucia, le principe est le même. Au fur et à mesure de l’histoire de GTA VI , les joueurs devront choisir quel type de personnages ils veulent incarner et décider si cette version de Jason et Lucia se dessine alors qu’ils sont ensemble ou si, au contraire, le mieux pour eux est qu’ils se séparent. Réponse le 19 novembre prochain.

With the calendar finally turning over to November, the long-awaited release of GTA 6 is finally within touching distance. Players have started making plans for November 19, including already booking days off work. Sick days to play the game might cost the US economy around $1.5 billion, too.
However, despite the release possibly affecting the economy, finance expert Mark Tilbury believes it could save players around $5000 each.
In his October 31 video, the self-made millionaire noted that if the game takes 80 hours to complete, it’ll cost you around $1.25 per hour, but that could drop as low as 50 cents once you start adding in free roaming.
“Let’s say you play for four hours every evening, that’s 50 nights of entertainment,” Tilbury added.
“Compare that to going out, where you could easily spend $100 in a single night, thats why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5000.”
Four hours of play each night is pretty conservative, seeing as people have waited over a decade for the game. Though, you won’t be able to speedrun through GTA 6 anyway.

GTA 6 Could Take Up 210GB on PS5, Nearly 50,000 MP3 Songs Could Fit in the Same Space Om Singh | November 3 | Industry & Events , Spotlight Share
Rockstar Games’ upcoming title GTA 6 could demand a substantial amount of storage space on gaming consoles, with a new leak suggesting that the game may require approximately 210GB for installation. If the information proves accurate, the highly anticipated title could occupy a significant portion of the storage available on a standard PlayStation 5.
The reported download size also offers an interesting comparison with the gaming and digital entertainment landscape of 2010. Back then, 200GB was enough to accommodate dozens of popular PC games or even tens of thousands of MP3 music tracks. Today, a single upcoming game could potentially require almost the same amount of space.
GTA 6 is scheduled to release on November 19, 2026, following a wait of 13 years since the previous mainline instalment in the franchise. With players preparing to return to Vice City, storage requirements could become another consideration before the game’s launch.
The reported 210GB download size originated from a leak shared by X user @PlayStation Size . Gaming publication Insider Gaming has also reported on the claim.
However, Rockstar Games has not officially confirmed the game’s final download size. The figure should therefore be treated as an unverified estimate rather than an established requirement.
If the reported size turns out to be accurate, GTA 6 could consume roughly one-fourth of the PlayStation 5’s advertised 825GB storage capacity. That could leave considerably less room for players who maintain a large collection of installed games.
The actual amount of usable storage on a console also differs from its advertised capacity, making the available space an important consideration.
The reported storage requirement becomes particularly interesting when compared with the size of popular games from earlier years.
In 2010, a 200GB drive could accommodate multiple copies of games that were widely played during that period. The original PC version of GTA Vice City required approximately 1.55GB of hard drive space, while GTA San Andreas needed around 4.7GB.
Other popular titles were similarly smaller in size. Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005) required approximately 3GB, while GTA III could run with around 500MB of storage.
These comparisons highlight how dramatically game storage requirements have changed over the years.
Gaming was not the only area where 200GB offered considerably more storage capacity in 2010. Digital music collections were also much easier to accommodate.
An average MP3 song could take approximately 4MB of storage space. Based on that estimate, a 200GB drive could theoretically hold close to 50,000 songs.
This makes the reported GTA 6 requirement particularly striking. The storage space that could once accommodate an enormous music collection or dozens of older games might now be needed for a single modern gaming title.
While the 210GB figure remains unconfirmed, the leak has brought attention to an increasingly important aspect of modern gaming: the amount of storage required to install and maintain major releases.

Quels sont les meilleurs personnages de la saga GTA ? Voici notre top, du pire protagoniste, au meilleur de la saga !
Dernière ligne droite avec la sortie de GTA 6 . Le 19 novembre, nous allons avoir l’occasion de découvrir deux nouveaux héros dans la série Grand Theft Auto . Un véritable événement, quand on sait à quel point Rockstar apporte un soin à l’écriture de ses personnages. Le moment idéal pour réaliser un classement des meilleurs protagonistes de la saga !
Bien entendu, nous ne prendrons pas en compte différents personnages comme les modèles prédéfinis du premier GTA et des extensions GTA London 1969 & GTA London 1961 . Ni les personnages des versions portables dans GTA Advance et GTA Chinatown Wars , puisque ce sont es personnages qui ne sont pas doublés . Nous allons nous concentrés sur les opus et les personnages principaux.
On commence ce top par Claude Speed. Le seul personnage muet de la saga, et forcément, cela n’aide pas à gagner en charisme. En plus de cela, Claude est clairement le personnage à tout faire de Liberty City. Personne ne lui accorde de respect, il n’a pas de caractère, il subit simplement son aventure, et parvient, tant bien que mal, à se venger de manière un peu inespérée. On l’aperçoit dans GTA San Andreas en 2004 et là encore, cela confirme que Claude est plus une victime, qu’un héros.
Alors, pour sa défense, Claude n’a pas eu le droit à la moindre ligne de dialogue dans les équipes n’ont pas eu le temps de lui écrire des répliques. À la base, GTA III devait être un remake du premier opus , donc il ne devait pas avoir de scénario. On devait simplement enchaîner les missions que différents personnages devaient nous donner via des cabines téléphoniques. C’est au dernier moment que Rockstar North a voulu intégrer une histoire au jeu.
C’est pourquoi les missions ne se suivent pas toujours avec logique et que Claude ne prononce pas le moindre mot . Comme dans GTA et GTA 2 , le joueur devait simplement écouter les consignes des missions et les exécuter. Rockstar n’a pas eu le temps de caster un acteur ni d’écrire des lignes de dialogues. Tant pis pour Claude !
En dixième position, Toni Cipriani, le héros de GTA Liberty City Stories en 2005 sur PSP. De base, Toni Cipriani est un homme de main à Salvatore Leone dans GTA III . Le jeu se déroulant deux ans plus tôt , on découvre comment Toni s’est rapproché de la Mafia. Et, clairement, c’est loin d’être le meilleur personnage. Dans GTA III déjà, il est un personnage secondaire déplorable.
C’est un personnage avec peu d’assurance, qui se fait marcher dessus, qui a du mal à obtenir le respect et qui a de lourds soucis émotionnels et psychiatriques qui tendent vers le côté psychopathe. Niveau charisme, il a du mal à en imposer également. Il surpasse tout de même Claude, car certaines de ses répliques sont pas mal, mais il est loin de pouvoir rivaliser avec les grands noms de la saga.
Franklin, c’est clairement le maillon faible du trio de GTA V . Au début du jeu, on découvre un jeune de la rue, qui semble avoir une certaine classe. Très vite, on se rend compte que ce n’est pas vraiment le digne héritier de CJ en termes de gangsta. Son histoire avec Tanisha tout au long du récit montre un homme assez faible, incapable de prendre des décisions et de gérer sa relation, qui se fait marcher dessus et mener par le bout du nez à de nombreuses reprises.
C’est un homme de la rue, qui n’assume plus ce rôle et qui souhaite en sortir. La série de braquage de GTA V lui permet de se payer une villa de luxe et de sortir de cette rue, pour une autre classe sociale dont il n’a pas les codes. Franklin est toujours dans une entre deux et peine à trouver sa place. Au final, on reste avec un personnage qui peine à vraiment trouver un style, un genre, une place. Ni bon ni mauvais, il est assez moyen dans l’histoire de GTA V . Il ne s’impose pas, et ne parvient pas à trouver le respect auquel il aspire. Ni par Tanisha, ni par ses anciens potes de la rue, dont Lamar. Et pour se faire manque de respect par Lamar, il en faut !

articles.txt:
Comme l'ensemble de la rédaction de Gamekult, je dois dire que je suis loin de vouer un culte au dieu GTA. Je ne vais pas vous faire l'historique, mais j'ai notamment snobé le phénomène au temps de la PS2. Et si GTA 6 m'intéresse clairement pour la démesure que le projet incarne et parce que j'ai envie de voir jusqu'où une équipe aux moyens virtuellement illimités peut pousser le souci du détail et la matière organique dans un monde ouvert, je peine à ressentir la même excitation que nombre de mes compatriotes joueurs. Alors pour donner du carburant à cette hype qui me fait défaut, et aussi parce que je n'ai pas trouvé de meilleures idées pour contribuer au trou noir médiatique , j'ai rallumé GTA 5 pour la toute première fois depuis septembre 2013.
Bon, évidemment, je n'ai pas poussé le vice (City) jusqu'à dépoussiérer une PS3 pour me replonger dans les conditions de l'époque, ce n'était pas le but. C'est donc bien sur PS5 que j'ai renoué avec Michael, Trevor et Franklin, deux générations plus tard. Depuis 2013, le jeu a été bien optimisé techniquement. Et c'est sans doute ce qui explique pourquoi mes sensations ont été meilleures que celles que j'avais eues en 2013. À la sortie du jeu sur PS3, je me souviens très bien avoir été surpris par cette lourdeur pénible dans chacun des déplacements des personnages. D'où ma surprise en découvrant une prise en main encore un peu molle au démarrage, mais relativement souple et dotée d'un système de couverture qui fonctionne. Marteler la touche X pour courir est en revanche aussi dépassé que peu instinctif, mais à part ça, GTA 5 a mieux vieilli que je ne l'imaginais. Tant qu'on y joue sur une machine récente, s'entend.
L'accumulation de tutoriels au cours de ce prologue nuit au rythme, certes, mais on n'a pas trouvé meilleur moyen d'apprendre les bases au joueur que de le faire démarrer au cœur de l'action. Je serais vraiment étonné que GTA 6 ne commence pas lui aussi par un flashback en nous lâchant au milieu d'un braquo. Peut-être pour nous montrer comment Lucia a fini en tôle ? Moins surprenant, le fait que GTA 5 tienne encore très bien la route dans sa mise en scène, ses transitions et la fluidité naturelle de ses dialogues. La densité du trafic routier est épatante, mais c'est un élément que Rockstar a optimisé en passant successivement le jeu sur PS4 et sur PS5.
En revanche, même si Rockstar avait atteint des sommets pour l'époque, la densité et la diversité de la population de GTA 5 ressemble soudainement à un brouillon par rapport à l'incroyable sensation de profusion et la diversité des personnages qu'on a pu voir dans les images et les vidéos de GTA 6 . Je confesse avoir maté l'une des fameuses fuites de Cyberleek. Cette vidéo montre Lucia, nue comme un ver pour l'occasion, agresser une pauvre citoyenne au hasard alors que celle-ci est train de retirer de l'argent au distributeur. À bientôt 44 ans et 7 générations de consoles dans les pattes, je ne pense pas être facile à impressionner sur le plan technique. Mais là, entre l'intensité du regard agacé de la jeune femme, le mouvement de ses tresses et le niveau des expressions faciales... Le fait d'imaginer qu'un simple PNJ parmi les milliers que l'on va croiser dans le jeu puisse avoir ce niveau de présence fait presque froid dans le dos.
Sur ce point, donc, il est clair que Rockstar est allé plus loin dans le détail que n'importe quel autre studio avant lui, au point de ringardiser la population qui circule dans Los Santos. À en croire Rockstar, une équipe entière s'est aussi attelée à l'élaboration des dialogues de PNJ que l'on peut écouter en tendant l'oreille, dans le respect de la distance sociale. Et comme on l'a appris récemment, les habitants de Leonida ne détaleront pas systématiquement comme des lapins à cause du mauvais comportement du joueur : face à des attaques gratuites ou sous la menace d'une arme, certains auront apparemment du répondant (et des armes). J'attends donc une profonde amélioration de tout ce qui donne lieu au « monde vivant », un endroit dans lequel on en arrive à perdre de vue son objectif pour se laisser simplement emporter par ce qu'il se passe autour.
Côté interface, on reprend ses marques assez vite avec l'emblématique menu circulaire, qui sera toujours là dans GTA 6 . Mais ce dernier proposera une séparation entre armes et objets, ainsi que des raccourcis pour les soins et le changement vestimentaire (qui prend tout son sens avec le nouveau système de police, on en reparle plus loin)

articles.t: Walmart’s ‘GTA 6’ preorder bonus leaked: How to score the surprise and delight bag
articles.chapeau: Walmart is trying to get you to buy a disc-less box.
articles.txt:
I just found out that preordering a physical copy of GTA 6 doesn't come with a game disc. You probably knew this already, but you just get a case with a digital voucher slip, meaning you will still need to clear a monstrous 210GB of SSD storage and wait out a massive download queue before stepping foot in Leonida.
I ditched my console a few years ago ( GTA 6 might persuade me to jump back in), so I'm not exactly the most clued-up gamer, but that feels a little silly to me. What is convincing shoppers to buy a plastic case without an actual disc?
Spotted by the deal-tracking account Nintendeals, Walmart apparently posted a product listing promising a complimentary "surprise and delight bag" bundled with every GTA 6 preorder ($79.99 at Walmart) .
I guess getting free swag with an $80 purchase that virtually never sees day-one discounts is a harmless win.
Walmart has history here. It offered promotional snack kits featuring Pringles and Coca-Cola bundled with last year's Nintendo Switch 2 preorders. Getting a novelty can of chips and promotional stickers is not really a compelling reason to buy a plastic case with a paper code inside, but maybe I am simply an old man yelling at a cloud.
If you actually want physical collector memorabilia, Rockstar is selling a separate $400 Collector's Box . The 11-piece crate packs custom Oakley sunglasses, a New Era cap, and a physical map of Leonida. But the actual game is sold separately, if you can believe it.

All GTA 6 leaks so far Discuss Now GTA 6 has had several leaks (Image via Rockstar Games) GTA 6 is right around the corner, and while the wait is certainly almost over, what a ride it has been. The game’s long waiting period was marred by leaks over the years, with everything coming to a climax with the infamous Cyberleek situation. The leaks drip-fed us information about the game, its characters, Vice City itself, and more.
If you’re eagerly waiting for GTA 6 to release and want a trip down memory lane about all the leaks, we have you covered. In this article, we’ll go over all the GTA 6 leaks that we’ve seen so far. Naturally, there may be some spoilers, so if you wish to walk into the game completely blind, you’ve been warned.
The first big GTA 6 leak came at the hands of a GTAForums user named Teapotuberhacker on September 18, 2022. The user leaked files showcasing an early build of the game , giving us our first look at the dual protagonists, Lucia and Jason. The leak also gave us glimpses of the new in-development Vice City , as well.
The next big leak came only a few months later, on December 2, 2023, mere days before the first trailer of the game. The leak was made by a TikToker named azzarossi, who was rumored to be the son of a Rockstar North employee . The leak gave us a glimpse of Vice City's skyscrapers and residential areas, as well as a busy highway.
With Rockstar's marketing going all in to build up the big Trailer 1 release on December 4, 2023, people were eagerly waiting to get their first official glimpse at the game. Well, some people got that glimpse early thanks to a leak of the entire trailer ahead of the official release. The leaked trailer, rumoured to have been released by a YouTube employee , forced Rockstar's hand and led to the official trailer being released early.
Fast forward to January 1, 2025, and we got a new leak on Reddit. User JustLovett0 shared an image he claimed was from "mid 2021." Furthermore, the user shared a Google Drive link that contained an image of Lucia on a monitor . Next to the monitor was a PS5 development kit , and an Xbox development kit was seen in another video. The office scenery also visually aligned with Rockstar San Diego's, adding credence to the leaks.
A week later, another Reddit user, Pebblestar_, shared in-game information he claimed was legitimate. According to the user, GTA 6 would feature crash physics resembling real-life crashes , multiple weapon wheels for weapons and attachments, high levels of gore , and allow players to enter 40% of the buildings on the map.
On September 8, 2025, dataminer Tez2 revealed that Take-Two Interactive had registered domains for in-game websites . The websites — what-up.app, rydeme.app, buckme.app, leonidagov.org, brianandbradley.com, and more — appeared to be websites you could visit in GTA 6. However, the very next day, Tez2 reported that all of the discovered domains had been removed from Take-Two’s nameservers.
Later, on November 30, 2025, a demo reel from former Rockstar Toronto character animator Benjamin Chue leaked on Vimeo. The demo reel showed off the game's animations, showing the player character using a bike. The demo reel was later taken down.

articles.chapeau: GTA 6 PS5 install size is reportedly 210GB, about 31% of a launch PS5 usable 667GB. Rockstar has not confirmed. Storage math and pre-load tips.
articles.txt:
Marcus Chen November 2, 2026 11 min read Grand Theft Auto VI may need more than 200GB on PlayStation 5, and the number has players checking their drives 17 days before launch. According to Gizbot , the X account PlayStation Game Size pulled the figure from Sony’s database, and Rockstar Games has not confirmed it. Times Now ran the story with a twist, asking what the same storage space could hold back in 2010.
The figure that keeps circulating is 210GB. That is a leak, not a spec sheet, and our GTA 6 confirmed-versus-rumor scorecard treats it the same way. This analysis walks through what was reported, what the PS5 can actually hold, what it means for storage buyers, and which parts of the story still lack proof.

Multiple outlets reported the same core claim in the last week of October 2026. Grand Theft Auto VI shows a download size of roughly 210GB on PlayStation 5, according to data tied to Sony’s PlayStation backend. OC3D described the game as having a 200+ GB download on PS5, with PlayStation Game Size reporting 210GB.
The word “reportedly” carries real weight here. Nobody has shown a Rockstar-published requirement, and no store listing we could verify carries one. Every number in this piece traces back to a leak or a third-party report. We flag that every time it matters, because storage numbers shape buying decisions and a wrong one costs people money.
The story fits the current rhythm of GTA 6 coverage. Launch is set for November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and every few days a new leak lands. Some hold up and many do not. We tested one batch in our look at the 25-minute leak and what holds up , and the storage claim deserves the same skeptical read.
The original source is the X account PlayStation Game Size, which tracks changes to Sony’s PlayStation database. The German outlet Playfront wrote that the account extracted the install size from the PSN database and tied it to a pre-load date of November 12. Gizbot, OC3D and Playfront all repeat the 200GB-plus framing, and most cite the same origin.
That matters for how you weigh the evidence. Ten articles repeating one tweet are still one data point. The account has a track record of reading store backend entries, which gives the claim more weight than a random forum post. Yet a backend entry is a snapshot. Publishers adjust packaging before launch, and a number visible today can change after a day-one patch.
Our confidence rating is moderate. The figure likely reflects a real database entry. Whether it reflects the final installed footprint is a separate question, and we cover it below.
Rockstar has not announced an install or download size for any platform. VGKami checked the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store and Rockstar support pages as of October 26, 2026 and found platforms and editions listed with no storage requirement. The 200GB and 210GB figures remain unconfirmed by the studio.
Rockstar tends to stay quiet until the last moment. The studio has also called leaks hard to handle, a point we covered when it said GTA 6 leaks feel invasive ahead of the November 19 launch . Expect an official number only when the store pages get their final specs.

articles.txt:
GTA 6: All details revealed so far Every major GTA 6 leak, Rockstar's confirmed details and the rumors still unproven ahead of 19 November
GTA 6 is 17 days away, and the gap between what Rockstar has confirmed and what the internet has made up has never been wider. Thirteen years after GTA 5, the game has survived two delays, a wave of stolen footage and a rumour mill that runs daily.
Here's what's official, what's leaked and what's still guesswork.
Grand Theft Auto VI is set to be released on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Initially, its release was scheduled for 2025, then moved to May 2026, and finally, November.
The CEO of Take-Two has reaffirmed the new date, with pre-orders, a preload schedule, and a launch trailer already made available. Nothing in the information found suggests a further postponement.
The Standard Edition is priced at $79.99, and the Ultimate Edition at $99.99. Purchase or preorder either of these editions until November 20 and receive the Vintage Vice City Pack as well. Preorder digitally and receive an additional bonus of a free one-month subscription to GTA+.
Boxed versions of the game will have a downloadable code only and not the disc itself. You will be able to purchase them starting November 12 to preload the game.
Preloading opens on November 12, a week before launch, for digital pre-orders and boxed copies. The files stay locked until November 19. Rockstar has given the date but not the exact unlock time, so check your console store's countdown.
How big is the download? Rockstar hasn't said. A figure of about 210GB is circulating, but it isn't official. Free up plenty of space before the 12th.
Not officially. Rockstar has announced PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only. On October 13 GamesBeat reported, citing four anonymous sources, that a PC version is planned for the first quarter of 2027. Rockstar hasn't commented.
GTA 5 reached consoles in September 2013 and PC in April 2015. And if you were hoping to stream it on PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming, Xbox's Matthew Ball denied that on October 7.
The Extended Look for August 27 featured a 26-minute-long video on Netflix and YouTube. As Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two criminals, you get to operate in the state of Leonida, where Vice City replaces Miami.
The details have been further expanded in the 430th issue of Edge magazine, available since October 29. The map is about twice the size of that of GTA 5 and with narrower streets and longer days. The police create a profile of you based on your car, clothing and accomplices, so car changes and wardrobe changes really do count.
There is a new criminal profile that evaluates your actions from "Professional" to "Irredeemable". Car stealing became more difficult, as some stolen cars come with trackers.
The leaks began on August 18, when a group calling itself Cyberleek posted gameplay clips and map images. Take-Two began takedowns and sought data from Microsoft and Discord to trace the source. Rockstar later apologised to fans and called the leaks heartbreaking.
On October 8, a roughly 25-minute clip followed. Rockstar hasn't commented on it, and its authenticity is unverified. Press reports say the leaked material appears to come from an older build, so it may not reflect the finished game. One analysis put the drop in Take-Two's market value at around $2.8 billion in two days.
It contains spoilers and explicit scenes, and pages offering a "GTA 6 download" are not official.
The next real answers arrive on 12 November, when preloads open and the store pages show the final file size.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leak 13: Beach Gameplay and Prologue Spoilers [2026]
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 Leak 13 showed Vice City beach gameplay on Aug. 25. See how the Cyberleek story unfolded and what to expect in the final 18 days.
articles.txt:
Nadia Dubois November 1, 2026 12 min read The 13th GTA 6 leak put a crowded Vice City beach on screen on August 25, 2026. Protagonist Jason rides a bike across the sand, stops near clusters of NPCs, and the camera shows crowds stretching toward the horizon. GameRant and RockstarINTEL both covered the clip the day it surfaced, and Forbes described the run of daily clips as hitting a full week.
Today is November 1, and GTA 6 is 18 days from its November 19 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. A lot has changed since Leak 13. Our earlier Cyberleek explainer tracks the full run of clips, and this article goes deeper on the beach leak, the prologue poll that followed it, and where the story stands now.
One correction up front. The beach clip and the prologue poll are not breaking news this morning. They date to late August. What makes them worth revisiting is how the campaign escalated afterward, and how little of it has been confirmed by Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive. This is a news analysis of that arc, with every number tied to a named outlet.
· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions.
According to GameRant, which published its write-up on August 25, the clip is gameplay footage of Jason riding a bike along a Vice City beach. He stops occasionally to look at groups of NPCs. The outlet noted that you can hear the NPCs holding conversations as Jason passes, that some stand in small clusters, and that a few of them hold cellphones in a way that reads as realistic.
RockstarINTEL titled its coverage around the same point: the leak shows an incredible number of NPCs. Fan accounts put the visible crowd at somewhere between a hundred and two hundred figures across the sand and in the water. That count is an eyeball estimate, not a Rockstar spec, so treat it as a rough scale rather than a technical claim. Umbrellas and other beach structures fill the background.
The choice of scene matters. Crowd density is one of the hardest things for an open-world game to fake, because every extra pedestrian costs animation, audio, and AI budget. A beach at sunset is close to a stress test. Our look at the reported 600,000 NPC animations covers the engineering side of why that crowd behavior is a big deal.
Cyberleek did not pick the scene alone. GameRant reported that the leaker had run an earlier poll asking followers to choose between a nudist town, a strip club, and a beach. The nudist town won the vote, yet fans argued that the beach would show off NPC density better. The beach clip landed as Leak 13.
That detail tells you something about the strategy. The leaks were not a one-off data dump. They worked as a serialized release, with audience votes steering each drop. Polls keep followers engaged, give every clip a built-in news hook, and let the leaker claim that fans, not the leaker, chose what to publish.
The pattern also made each leak easy to cover. Outlets such as GameRant, Kotaku, and Forbes could report the next poll, then the clip that followed, then the reaction. A daily cadence with a vote attached produces a news cycle on demand. Whether that counts as protest or promotion is a question we return to in the memecoin section below.
The headline threat attached to Leak 13 was the next poll. GameRant reported that Cyberleek was asking followers whether to leak the prologue featuring Lucia, and that the vote was leaning toward yes when the beach story ran. Fans speculated that the leaker had access to a restricted build containing only the prologue. That theory is a fan inference, not a confirmed fact.
Kotaku reported on August 26 that the leaker had begun sharing story spoilers. The footage appeared to be the game’s opening prologue, with Lucia in prison, the same setting as the official 2023 debut trailer. Kotaku said she wears an orange jumpsuit and that additional backstory details were revealed. The poll that looked like a threat on August 25 had become a leak by the next day.
Gameplay clips show mechanics. Story clips show plot. Spoilers hit harder, because a player cannot unsee an opening sequence, and Rockstar builds its marketing around narrative reveals. Kotaku said the leaker included a message claiming the build is recent and that the game is not ready. That is Cyberleek’s claim. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has verified it, and the reported release date has not moved.
Forbes columnist Paul

Un rapport de Tom Warren pour The Verge évoque The Elder Scrolls 6 Sentinel, attendu à Hammerfell, avec un récit bien plus centré sur les Parchemins Anciens. Que cache vraiment cette fuite qui enflamme les fans de lore depuis la promesse d’une annonce en novembre 2026 ?
Selon une nouvelle fuite très commentée, le prochain épisode de la saga se nommerait officiellement The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel , avec une intrigue centrée sur l’histoire même des Parchemins Anciens. Un rapport signé par le journaliste Tom Warren affirme que Bethesda Game Studios préparerait un scénario qui mettrait enfin ces artefacts au cœur du jeu, et non plus en simple prétexte de quête secondaire.
Depuis le teaser E3 2018, les fans dissèquent la moindre image à la recherche d’indices, jusqu’à traquer le mot « SENTINEL » dans un identifiant caché de Starfield . Cette fuite est la première à décrire une véritable direction narrative pour The Elder Scrolls 6 , et elle pourrait bien changer les attentes de tous ceux qui rêvent d’un épisode ultra axé sur le lore.
Dans sa newsletter datée du 29 octobre 2026, Tom Warren explique, en citant des sources proches des plans de Bethesda Game Studios, que le jeu porterait le titre The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel et se déroulerait à Hammerfell , appelée Lenclume en français. Les joueurs y retrouveraient la grande cité portuaire de Sentinel , royaume rougegarde dominant la baie d’Iliac dans l’univers de Tamriel.
Le point clé du rapport, repris par plusieurs sites spécialisés, tient en une phrase. Selon Warren, il s’agirait « du premier jeu consacré à l’histoire des Elder Scrolls, qui aidera à lever le voile sur les secrets de ces mystérieux artefacts anciens ». Autrement dit, les Parchemins Anciens ne seraient plus seulement l’objet que l’on va chercher au fond d’un donjon, mais le sujet central de l’intrigue.
Cette orientation colle aux indices semés depuis des années. Un tweet d’Asha Sharma montrant « The Elder Scrolls VI: ******** » a poussé la communauté à deviner « Sentinel », tandis que le teaser de 2018 pointait déjà vers les paysages côtiers et désertiques de Lenclume, terre des Rougegardes .
Dans le lore, les Parchemins Anciens sont une sorte de codex vivant de l’univers, des textes prophétiques capables de déformer le temps et la mémoire de ceux qui les lisent. Dans Oblivion ou The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , ils ont pesé sur la trame principale, mais restaient un outil scénaristique parmi d’autres.
Faire de cet héritage le cœur de The Elder Scrolls 6 Sentinel signifie potentiellement un jeu plus mystique, où visions, prophéties et réécriture de l’histoire de Tamriel occupent le devant de la scène. Les quêtes pourraient davantage tourner autour d’artefacts magiques, de sectes érudites et de conflits entre ceux qui veulent exploiter ces textes et ceux qui cherchent à les protéger.
Placée dans les déserts, ruines anciennes et ports stratégiques de Hammerfell , cette intrigue offrirait un terrain idéal pour un jeu de rôle « classic Bethesda » mêlant exploration de donjons enfouis, politique locale de Sentinel et enjeux métaphysiques liés aux Parchemins Anciens.
La même fuite évoque une révélation officielle du titre en novembre 2026, période qui coïnciderait avec les quinze ans de Skyrim , sorti le 11 novembre 2011. Les sources parlent surtout d’un dévoilement du nom et de l’orientation de l’histoire, sans garantie de gameplay ni de fenêtre de sortie, et aucun prix n’a été mentionné.
En interne, une présentation jouable aurait eu lieu en août 2026. Asha Sharma, responsable Xbox, y aurait décrit une histoire « encore plus grandiose », ce qui laisse entendre que Microsoft mise fortement sur l’ampleur narrative de The Elder Scrolls 6 Sentinel , au moins autant que sur sa taille de carte.
Reste que tout cela demeure non confirmé. Tom Warren est une voix solide dans l’écosystème tech, et les détails qu’il avance s’alignent avec les clins d’œil observés dans Starfield , mais Bethesda Game Studios n’a encore rien officialisé. Si la fuite se vérifie, les fans de lore peuvent toutefois s’attendre à un épisode qui regarde moins vers la politique façon Skyrim et davantage vers la magie, les mythes et les secrets les plus anciens de Tamriel.
